text:
Charlotte,

I asked Will to take a look around at your documentation and check out the product. It seems to be missing a key data modality (time series) which is of critical importance to us. Beyond this, i have also spoken with German and understand that he has moved on to another product due to missing functionality and cost. At this point, we use LabelStudio and are quite happy with it and don’t see Encord as having a compelling enough feature set to drive us to change.

Furthermore, while I understand the sales hustle, I (and I suspect most) do not appreciate or respond well to being called, unsolicited, on my personal cell phone.

Best
Robert.

subject: Re: Recap | Bloomfield - Encord
text:
Thanks Leo for the introduction!

Hi Skander, nice meeting you!

Thanks, I am available for 30 minutes at 6:30. Please invite
jasmine.ortega@bloomfield.ai, anna@bloomfield.ai and
shreya.kale@bloomfield.ai as well.

To give you some context, we have identified annotation quality issues in
our blueberry instance segmentation datasets. Many blueberries are
misclassified (assigned to the wrong color). We would like to easily review
and re-annotate this data.  These datasets are containing thousands of
blueberries in each image, each classified for a primary and a secondary
color.

Here is a list of the subjects we would like to discuss:

   - patch view to review segmented object annotation for each label or
   tags (please find attached an example screenshot from the voxel51 feature
   we are interested in) or the equivalent feature you have
   - object detection/ segmentation embedding visualisation (and use it to
   select object annotations to review using patch view)
   - patch view to review segmented object for ground-truth label/
   prediction comparisons (a good use case for us would be to review all
   blueberries annotated as green but classified as pink for example)
   - loading into encord instance segmentation data containing a bitmap for
   each instance or a polygon for each instance (we particularly use the later
   for overlapping detections, typically a cluster and its berries)

Best,

Jean
